question: Within Peromyscus populations, does higher same-genus MNKA produce smaller raw nearest-neighbor trap-centroid spacing but more positive local-spacing excess than expected from geometry and repeat-supported cohort sampling?

new_response.source: NEON small mammal standardized three-night plot-events NOT present in RELEASE-2026
new_response.taxon: Peromyscus (same protocol target taxon concepts, original genus-MNKA rules)
new_response.geometry: same 10 x 10 lattice, coordinates A1..J10; three nights; >=5 repeat-supported individuals
new_response.period: first future release(s) attaining the fixed estimability gate; stop and report support-only if not estimable
new_response.null_A: 199 fixed-seed x-y reassignment replicates per session preserving m and B_observed exactly
new_response.null_B: 199 without-replacement draws of m other-event same-taxon-plot centroids, using future-only sessions; no reuse of RELEASE-2026 centroids in response or null reference

effect_blind_support_gate.if_failed: INCONCLUSIVE_SUPPORT_STOP, do not lower thresholds or append RELEASE-2026 response

prospective_tests.model: taxon x plot fixed effects, site x calendar-month fixed effects and calendar-year fixed effects where identifiable in the frozen future data
prospective_tests.weighting: equal session weights within Peromyscus genus; report heterogeneity across taxon concepts
prospective_tests.decision: require both primary slope coefficients positive, and site-cluster bootstrap lower 95% interval above zero for both; bootstrap fixed B=2000, seeded, resample sites

causal_boundary.claim_if_passed: prospectively replicated, observation-conditioned local spatial regularity association with genus-level MNKA in Peromyscus
exclude_rescues: switch to other genus after Peromyscus failure
select null simulations conditional on future sign
